name: Silt Strider default acquisition policy
notes: Authored rules, versioned independently of any extraction snapshot.
Changing a rule here never requires re-extracting the game data.
Thresholds are stated once; the evaluator derives numbers from the game.
Worn gear is priced pro rata: a CellRef condition of 2 of 300 is worth 27 gold.
Broken gear counts: condition 0 is free and repairable, so it is a route, not protection. The optimizer must repair before it is armour.
The gold cap applies to purchases only. Theft that clears the danger and lock rules has no price limit, because nothing is being paid.
Samarys is a starting-area place: the benchmark item must pass its own benchmark.

Faction-owned items are theft for a level 1 character, who belongs to no faction yet: Redoran's vaults and the Imperial Cult's chapels hold plenty of loose gear, and taking it is a crime until you join and rise far enough. assumeFactionAccess was true until 2026-09-27, which offered those as free.

endgame.boundSummons: an item whose Cast When Used enchantment conjures Bound gear is endgame, whatever it costs. The Devil, Demon and Fiend weapons are priced like steel and conjure a Bound weapon that hits like Daedric: a 157 gold Devil Tanto gives a Bound Dagger to match a 14,000 gold Daedric Tanto, five 60-second casts per charge. Gear rows rank such a weapon on what it conjures in its own skill, and armour on a conjured piece for its own slot.

holdingCellPrefixes: Tamriel Rebuilt's TR_Hold_ cells are hidden storage for scripts, quest rewards and staged NPCs, with no door in. TR_HOLD_Firewatch Ext Merchants holds a whole market, stalls and merchants, that no script moves out yet. Nothing there is reachable, bought or taken. Ships' cargo holds are real places and are not matched.

A merchant sells what they own only while standing near it: OpenMW's trade window offers their inventory plus the containers and loose items they own in the active cells (World::getContainersOwnedBy, getItemsOwnedBy), so the same interior or, outside, the neighbouring cells. Stock they own anywhere else is never offered, and taking it is theft.
A purchase ignores the lock on the chest a merchant keeps stock in: the merchant hands it over. The doors in front of the merchant still count.

uniformScripts name item scripts that make the wearer an impostor. OrdinatorUniform sets WearingOrdinatorUni on equip, and Ordinators react to it (Tamriel Rebuilt exempts members of T_Mw_Ordinators). Only the helmets and cuirasses that carry the script are excluded; the rest of an Indoril set is safe to wear.

ambushes are gear worn by an actor a script sends at the player, offered only under its own site toggle. Rows for it name that toggle instead of the policy toggles. darkBrotherhood: Tribunal's dbAttackScript wakes a resting character to a Dark Brotherhood assassin; at levels 1 to 3 it places one db_assassin1b, level 1, wearing the whole set at 30 armour a piece. The builder checks the profile's winning script still places that actor. Only the armour is offered: the Silver Dagger is sold everywhere and the one Ebony Dart is one throw.
excludedCells lists exact keys: a substring match on 'test' would wrongly drop Nchuleftingth's Test of Pattern and Atestas' Pawn & Loan.

objectiveNotes.power: What the piece is for: armour rating on armour and shields, best damage on weapons, and on clothing its enchantment: an enchanted ring or amulet first, on what its enchantment is worth, then a blank one on its capacity. An enchantment settles a tie on armour and weapons.
objectiveNotes.enchantment: Enchantment capacity for your own enchantment, which decides what a constant effect can cost. Only a blank piece takes one, so every blank ranks before any enchanted piece. Often a different item from power: the best cuirass in the game has 100 armour at 1,500 points of room.

enchantmentUsefulness.note: How much each effect of a piece's own enchantment counts when a row ranks on it: its engine cost times its tier's weight. Essential effects keep a fighter or caster alive or hitting; situational ones help against some foes or in some places; convenience ones make travel or exploring easier; none never counts in an item's favour. A curse on the wearer counts in full against whatever its tier. An entry may name one attribute or skill, like "Fortify Attribute: Personality", to override its effect for that alone. Drafted 2026-09-27 and checked against community consensus: Resist Normal Weapons is situational (silver, Daedric and enchanted weapons ignore it), and a Drain on an enemy is convenience (it wears off; Damage Attribute lasts).

ambushes.label: Dark Brotherhood armor
ambushes.note: Worn by the Dark Brotherhood assassin Tribunal sends while you sleep. At levels 1 to 3 it is one level 1 assassin, a 20% chance each rest, 10% after the first attack and none after the second. Kill them for the whole set.
